NC 2026 Primary:
Unaffiliated Voter Ballot Choice by County

Which party ballot did unaffiliated voters choose?

Published

March 8, 2026

Data

In the March 3, 2026 primary, 215,488 unaffiliated voters cast either a Democratic or Republican ballot. Statewide, 56.1% chose the Democratic ballot and 43.9% chose the Republican ballot.

Do Unaffiliated Voters Vote Like Their County?

To test whether unaffiliated voters’ ballot choices track the partisan lean of their county, we merge the 2026 primary ballot data with the 2024 presidential two-party vote share by county.

Trump Vote Share vs. % Unaffiliated Choosing the Democratic Ballot

In counties where Trump ran strongest, unaffiliated voters overwhelmingly chose the Republican primary ballot. The relationship is strongly negative (R² = 0.627).

Trump Vote Share vs. % Unaffiliated Choosing the Republican Ballot

The mirror image: unaffiliated voters in Trump-heavy counties chose the Republican ballot at very high rates (R² = 0.627). The two R² values are identical because % DEM and % REP are complements — but seeing both plots drives the point home.

Combined View: UNA Ballot Margin vs. County Partisan Lean

This plot expresses the same relationship on a margin-vs-margin scale: counties in the lower-right (Republican-leaning counties where UNA voters picked Republican ballots) and upper-left (Democratic counties where UNA voters picked Democratic ballots) confirm that unaffiliated voters broadly mirror their county’s partisan lean.
